patch_description: The main cost per annealing step is a full O(286) triangle scan plus a Python-loop convex hull. Implement the incremental scheme: precompute, for each vertex i, the indices of the 66 triangles containing i and the 220 not containing i. When vertex i moves, only the 66 affected areas change; the min over the other 220 can be cached along with the hull area (only recompute the hull when the moved vertex was a hull vertex). This gives roughly a 4-10x per-move speedup, which converts directly into many more annealing moves within the 3s budget — the proven lever for score gains. Since a move only changes one point, we cache `min_rest` (min area over triangles not containing i) and `hull_area`; the candidate's min triangle area is min(min_rest, min over 66 affected triangles).
